problems.title: Positive regularization does not remove rank-cutoff ties
problems.source_location: Introduction, PDF p.2, first contribution bullet; Proposition 1 and Theorem 1
claim: The introduction claims a unique regularized rank-constrained solution for every calibration matrix \(X\).
analysis: For \(W=X=I_2\), rank budget \(1\) and \(\mu=1/2\), the objective is \(3\|I_2-W^\prime\|_F^2/2\). Both \(\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\), and every rank-one orthogonal projector, attain global minimum \(3/2\). The discarded singular-value bound proves optimality. Positive definite weighting does not make the rank-constrained feasible set convex.
result: The universal introductory statement is too strong. The gap-conditioned theorem and Proposition 1’s allowance of multiple solutions are explicit countercontrols.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: After the invertible rank-preserving change \(Y=W^\prime(XX^\top+\mu I)^{1/2}\), apply ordinary truncated SVD. At a nontrivial cutoff, uniqueness requires a strict gap in the weighted matrix’s singular values.
problems.impact_rationale: This corrects broad introductory wording while the main conditional theorem remains valid.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: The QR helper compares feature count with the wrong factor dimension
problems.source_location: Algorithm 1, PDF p.4; released lib/TSQR.py, qr_one_device, lines 38–77
claim: `lib/TSQR.py`, `qr_one_device`, compares a new block’s feature-row count with the intermediate reduced QR factor’s row count.
analysis: A full-row-rank \(4\)-by-\(5\) matrix may be split into \(4\)-by-\(2\) and \(4\)-by-\(3\) blocks. Reduced QR of the first transpose gives \(R_0\) of size \(2\)-by-\(4\). Comparing the next feature count \(4\) with its row count \(2\) rejects valid common-feature blocks. Stacking \(R_0\) with the next transpose is dimensionally valid.
result: The public helper rejects a valid streamed partition. A square-first-block control and a separate concatenation path can avoid it.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Compare against the factor’s column count or the saved feature count. The update then preserves \(R^\top R=\sum_iX_iX_i^\top\), including short initial blocks.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded helper bug, not failure of QR or the central approximation method.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
